messages:
erin: Nightly perf job flagged a regression in kernel selector on sm86 for seqlen ~512-768. Seems the picker flips from flash-v2 (fast) to an older non-causal fallback when head_dim crosses 48->56, causing ~18-25% p99 token latency increase. Paste of microprobe sample below. :eyes:

noah: Oof. Do we have a repro command?

erin: Yep repro steps:
```
# run on an sm86 instance
bench_kernel_picker 
  --model llama-70b 
  --arch sm86 
  --heads 56 
  --head-dim 64 
  --seqlen 640 
  --batch 1 
  --kv-cache true 
  --warmup 50 
  --iters 200
```
Profiler snippet (trimmed):
```
[seqlen=640, batch=1, heads=56, hd=64, kv=on]
selector: chose kernel=v1_slow_causal (why?)
micro-avg p50: 8.9ms -> expected 6.1ms
micro-avg p99: 26.3ms -> expected 20.1ms
kv-cache miss rate: 4.8% (spikes on initial tokens)
selector heuristics: seqlen_bucket=512-768, head_bucket=49-64 -> current score bias=+0.12 toward v1
```

kai: Interesting that bias number. Could be the scoring function overweights warp-occupancy for 56 heads on sm86 which penalizes flash-v2 tiled path. We recently tuned for sm90 and larger head dims, might have regressed older architectures.

julie: I can reproduce locally with microprobe and get similar p99. Also see more kernel handoffs when KV cache warms (first 30 tokens). Flamegraph shows repeated kernel switching which correlates with jank.

perf-bot: automated-test: nightly/kernel-selector-sm86-56hd FAILED (+22% p99) https://ci.redwood/inference/3421 :rotating_light:

erin: Quick diagnostic I ran: forced picker to pick flash-v2 for the bucket and p99 dropped back to ~19.8ms. So two things: scoring math or hysteresis window too small -> transient flips during early kv-cache misses.

noah: Repro confirms. Can we try increasing hysteresis threshold from 100ms -> 500ms or increase confidence margin for architecture-sm86 so it prefers flash-v2 unless score diff > 0.25?

kai: Proposed config diff (temporary) to test:
```
{
  "kernel_picker": {
    "hysteresis_ms": 500,
    "arch_overrides": {
      "sm86": { "min_score_delta": 0.25 }
    },
    "seqlen_bucket_thresholds": [128, 512, 1024]
  }
}
```
If that stabilizes the path, we can tweak scoring offline.

julie: Also want to try a KV warmup tweak: avoid re-evaluating selector for first 64 tokens when kv-cache steady-state not reached. Quick patch: skip_selector_probe_if(kv_hits < 0.95 && token_index < 64).

erin: Agreed. Two-pronged: (1) bump hysteresis + sm86 override; (2) add kv-warmup gating to selector probe. I'll open an issue and run canary with both.

kai: I opened GH issue #4123 and added test plan + perf numbers. Assigned to @julie for the gating patch and @erin for the config roll.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started for kernel-picker-config-2026-03-18 to pool:sm86-canary (3 nodes)

julie: Working on gating patch, will push a draft PR (link soon).

erin: Thanks. If canary looks good after 2 hours we can promote to stable. If not, rollback plan is to pin that bucket to flash-v2 and revert selector changes. :+1:
